code: library(exnexSurv) library(survival) library(ggplot2) library(bayesplot)  simulate_surv_data <- function(   theta,   sigma2,   beta = NULL,   n_per_group = 60,   censor_min = 4,   censor_max = 12,   seed = NULL ) {   if (!is.null(seed)) {     set.seed(seed)   }    groups <- rep(seq_along(theta), each = n_per_group)   age_std <- rnorm(length(groups), mean = 0, sd = 1)   mean_log_time <- rep(theta, each = n_per_group)    if (!is.null(beta)) {     mean_log_time <- mean_log_time + beta * age_std   }    log_time <- rnorm(length(groups), mean = mean_log_time, sd = sqrt(sigma2))   true_time <- exp(log_time)   censor_time <- runif(length(groups), min = censor_min, max = censor_max)    data.frame(     time = pmin(true_time, censor_time),     event = as.integer(true_time <= censor_time),     group = factor(groups),     age_std = age_std   ) }  sim_data <- simulate_surv_data(   theta = c(1.2, 1.7, 2.1),   sigma2 = 0.20,   beta = -0.35,   n_per_group = 60,   seed = 6841 )  mean(sim_data$event) #> [1] 0.6777778

title: The EXNEX Model, Priors, and Data Augmentation
text: Basket trials enroll patients several small groups (baskets), often defined biomarker, tumor histology, cancer type, studied common protocol. basket typically contains handful patients, separately estimating effect every basket imprecise, pooling patients single estimate ignores real differences baskets. Borrowing information across baskets strikes middle ground: baskets look alike share strength, baskets disagree majority allowed stand apart. EXNEX (Exchangeable–Non-Exchangeable) framework extends standard exchangeable hierarchical model attaching latent indicator every basket selects whether effect drawn shared exchangeable component basket-specific non-exchangeable prior [@neuenschwander2016]. exnexSurv implements EXNEX right-censored, log-normal survival data using data-augmented Gibbs sampler written C++ via Rcpp RcppArmadillo [@eddelbuettel2011rcpp; @sanderson2016armadillo]. vignette explains model, priors customize , data augmentation mechanism makes sampler exact fast, systematic Gibbs scan, fitted object contains. short worked example illustrates shrinkage prior customization. statistical methodology described detail companion paper (Ney, 2026); performance numbers quoted last section taken .

code: fit <- pooling_surv(   Surv(time, event) ~ group,   data = d,   priors = list(     p_mix  = 0.7,     v_nex  = 10,     a_tau  = 3,     b_tau  = 3,     v_beta = 10   ) ) library(exnexSurv) library(survival) library(ggplot2)  simulate_basket_data <- function(   theta,   sigma = 1.2,   beta = c(0.8, -0.5),   group_sizes = c(30, 24, 20, 16, 14, 11, 8, 7, 5),   target_cens = 0.30,   seed = 1 ) {   set.seed(seed)   K <- length(theta)   group <- rep(seq_len(K), times = group_sizes)   n <- length(group)   X1 <- rnorm(n)   X2 <- rnorm(n)   eta <- theta[group] + X1 * beta[1] + X2 * beta[2]   log_time <- eta + rnorm(n, 0, sigma)   true_time <- exp(log_time)   censor_fun <- function(c) mean(true_time > c) - target_cens   censor_time <- uniroot(censor_fun, c(min(true_time), max(true_time)))$root   data.frame(     time = pmin(true_time, censor_time),     event = as.integer(true_time <= censor_time),     group = factor(group),     X1 = X1,     X2 = X2   ) }  theta_true <- c(1.5, 1.4, 1.6, 1.45, 1.55, 1.5, -0.4, -0.6, -0.5) d <- simulate_basket_data(theta_true, seed = 1)  # small, quick fit just to inspect resolved_priors quick <- pooling_surv(   Surv(time, event) ~ group + X1 + X2,   data = d,   priors = list(p_mix = 0.7, v_nex = 10),   iter = 400, warmup = 200, chains = 1 ) print(quick$resolved_priors) #> $a_sigma #> [1] 2 #>  #> $b_sigma #> [1] 2 #>  #> $a_tau #> [1] 2 #>  #> $b_tau #> [1] 2 #>  #> $p_mix #> [1] 0.7 #>  #> $m_mu #> [1] 0 #>  #> $v_mu #> [1] 10000 #>  #> $m_nex #> [1] 0 #>  #> $v_nex #> [1] 10 #>  #> $v_beta #> [1] 10000

title: Pointwise log-likelihood and WAIC from an pooling_surv fit — compute_waic
text: observation \(\), posterior draws indexed \(s=1,\ldots,S\), compute pointwise log-likelihood \(\log p(y_i \mid \theta^{(s)})\), log-normal AFT model gives observed event (\(\delta_i=1\)) $$\log p(y_i \mid \theta^{(s)}) =   \log\phi\!\left(\frac{\log t_i-\eta_i^{(s)}}{\sigma^{(s)}}\right)   - \log(\sigma^{(s)} t_i),$$ censored observation (\(\delta_i=0\)) $$\log p(y_i \mid \theta^{(s)}) =   \log\!\left[1-\Phi\!\left(\frac{\log t_i-\eta_i^{(s)}}{\sigma^{(s)}}\right)\right],$$ \(\eta_i^{(s)}\) linear predictor built draws. WAIC $$lpd = \sum_i \log\!\left(\frac{1}{S}\sum_s \exp\log p(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})\right),$$ $$p_{waic} = \sum_i \mathrm{var}_s\big(\log p(y_i\mid\theta^{(s)})\big),$$ $$\mathrm{WAIC} = -2(lpd - p_{waic}).$$ Rows extreme leverage (`p_waic` large threshold) may flag issues; function returns `pointwise` matrix users can investigate.

title: Fit Bayesian Pooling Survival Models — pooling_surv
text: patient \(\), model $$\log T_i = \theta_{g[]} + X_i^{\mathsf T}\beta + \varepsilon_i,\quad \varepsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2),$$ argument pooling selects prior structure basket effects \(\theta_j\): "exnex" (default) latent EXNEX hierarchy,     $$\theta_j\mid Z_j\sim Z_j\,\mathcal N(\mu,\tau^2)     +(1-Z_j)\,\mathcal N(m_{0j},v_{0j}),\quad     Z_j\sim\mathrm{Bern}(p_{\mathrm{exch},j}),$$     basket either borrows strength exchangeable     component \(\mathcal N(\mu,\tau^2)\) follows     non-exchangeable prior \(\mathcal N(m_{0j},v_{0j})\). "complete" complete pooling: single shared basket effect     \(\theta_j=\theta\) baskets prior     \(\theta\sim\mathcal N(m_{\mu},v_{\mu})\). "none" pooling: independent basket effects,     \(\theta_j\sim\mathcal N(m_{0j},v_{0j})\) \(j=1,\dots,K\). first predictor variable model formula interpreted basket/group assignment; additional variables covariates linear predictor log-survival scale. Censored event times handled data augmentation: censored log-time imputed truncated-Normal conditional distribution (inverse-CDF log space) remaining parameters updated conjugate full conditionals. sampler keeps posterior draws \(\theta_j\), \(\beta\), \(\sigma^2\).

title: Fit Bayesian Pooling Survival Models — pooling_surv
code: # Small simulated dataset: three baskets, one covariate, ~25% censoring set.seed(1) n <- 90 group <- factor(rep(1:3, each = 30)) x1 <- rnorm(n) eta <- rep(c(1.1, 1.6, 2.0), each = 30) + 0.5 * x1 true_time <- exp(eta + rnorm(n, 0, 0.6)) cens_time <- runif(n, 2, 9) d <- data.frame(   time = pmin(true_time, cens_time),   event = as.integer(true_time <= cens_time),   group = group,   x1 = x1 )  # Fit the EXNEX hierarchy with group effects and one covariate fit <- pooling_surv(   survival::Surv(time, event) ~ group + x1,   data = d,   priors = list(p_mix = 0.7),   iter = 300, warmup = 150, chains = 1 ) print(fit, show_trace = FALSE) #> <pooling_surv model> #> Pooling: exnex  #> Draws: 150 total post-warmup samples #>        150 post-warmup samples per chain #> Groups: 3 | Covariates: 1  #> MCMC: iter = 300 , warmup = 150 , thin = 1 , chains = 1  #>  #>  parameter      mean         sd       q05       q50       q95     rhat ess_bulk #>    theta_1 1.2335895 0.13974939 1.0095657 1.2187444 1.4675805 1.016317 78.54732 #>    theta_2 1.4724191 0.13478558 1.2427548 1.4719397 1.6794470 1.002595 70.19314 #>    theta_3 2.1979588 0.15277914 1.9438532 2.1936782 2.4377354 1.003304 56.67331 #>     beta_1 0.5189845 0.08791554 0.3809179 0.5196996 0.6528267 1.016858 92.05982 #>     sigma2 0.4029807 0.08911116 0.2882274 0.3903261 0.5883140 1.014836 30.91370 #>   ess_tail #>  104.18341 #>   89.79518 #>  131.31411 #>  132.80604 #>   31.09511 #>  #> Convergence: max R-hat = 1.02 | min ESS = 30.9 (consider longer chains or more warmup) summary(fit) #>   parameter      mean         sd       q05       q50       q95     rhat #> 1   theta_1 1.2335895 0.13974939 1.0095657 1.2187444 1.4675805 1.016317 #> 2   theta_2 1.4724191 0.13478558 1.2427548 1.4719397 1.6794470 1.002595 #> 3   theta_3 2.1979588 0.15277914 1.9438532 2.1936782 2.4377354 1.003304 #> 4    beta_1 0.5189845 0.08791554 0.3809179 0.5196996 0.6528267 1.016858 #> 5    sigma2 0.4029807 0.08911116 0.2882274 0.3903261 0.5883140 1.014836 #>   ess_bulk  ess_tail #> 1 78.54732 104.18341 #> 2 70.19314  89.79518 #> 3 56.67331 131.31411 #> 4 92.05982 132.80604 #> 5 30.91370  31.09511  # text: Computes posterior survival curves \(S(t) = \Pr(T > t)\) fitted `pooling_surv` model log-normal AFT specification: $$\log T_i = \theta_{g[]} + X_i^\top\beta + \varepsilon,\qquad   \varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2).$$ fixed time \(t\) linear predictor \(\eta\), survival probability log-normal distribution $$S(t) = 1 - \Phi\!\left(\frac{\log t - \eta}{\sigma}\right),$$ \(\sigma^2\) residual variance. Posterior draws \((\theta, \beta, \sigma^2)\) propagated expression obtain full posterior distribution \(S(t)\) time point.

title: exnexSurv 1.4.0
text: exnex_surv() deprecated favour pooling_surv(); now emits one-line deprecation message forces pooling = "exnex". existing calls continue work. Fitted objects class "pooling_surv"; methods (summary(), print(), plot(), survival_curves(), median_survival(), rmst(), probability_superiority(), compute_waic(), compare_waic()) accept .

title: exnexSurv 1.4.0
text: Priors irrelevant chosen pooling mode (e.g. p_mix "complete" "none") now trigger warning naming ignored fields. print() output now labels fitted pooling variant. New thin argument pooling_surv(): keep every thin-th post-warmup draw (default 1, keep ). Thinning reduces memory posterior autocorrelation without changing sampler. New verbose argument pooling_surv() (default TRUE): live progress bar (progressr) reports progress chains run; silenced verbose = FALSE. compare_waic() now names rows argument names used call (e.g. fit_exnex) instead anonymous fit1/fit2 labels; informative name available falls back fitted pooling variant. parallel_chains pooling_surv() now logical flag: TRUE runs chains concurrently background sessions future framework (progress workers relayed console, works RStudio ); FALSE (default) runs chains sequentially. verbose = TRUE, live progress bar (progressr) now updates chains run, sequential parallel execution; per-chain text lines removed. New convergence_diagnostics() computes split R-hat, bulk ESS tail ESS per parameter; summary()/print() now include columns one-line convergence verdict automatically. New rank_probabilities() gives posterior probability rank position per basket (median survival, S(t_0), RMST summaries). New posterior_predictive_check() overlays posterior predictive mean survival curve observed Kaplan-Meier curve per basket. New shrinkage_plot() contrasts EXNEX posterior estimates unpooled Kaplan-Meier medians visualise partial pooling.
